bull_case: AI-driven ad ranking sustains strong monetization while infrastructure investment converts into revenue and operating leverage. Owner FCF/share recovers from the 2026 investment trough and reaches $79 by year 10; the locked DCF yields about $1,091/share.
bear_case: AI infrastructure remains structurally capital-intensive, ad growth decelerates faster than expected, and Reality Labs keeps consuming roughly $20B annually. Owner FCF/share rises only to $26 by year 10; the locked DCF yields about $267/share.
thesis: At $741.25, META remains below the locked Bull value (~$1,091) but is now materially above the unchanged Base value (~$638), with price/Base ≈ 1.161x. No new quarterly filing changed the owner-FCF scenario paths; the September 21 move therefore narrows the expectation gap versus the September 18 run.

evidence.claim: Meta reported 2025 operating cash flow of $115.8B and free cash flow of $43.585B versus $52.103B in 2024; the decline in FCF despite higher revenue establishes a real reinvestment burden rather than a purely accounting concern.
Q2 2026 revenue was $60.801B, up 28% YoY; ad impressions rose 14% and average price per ad rose 12%, indicating that both engagement/inventory and monetization were contributing to growth.
Q2 2026 operating cash flow was $31.862B but company-defined FCF was only $0.784B after $31.08B of capex including finance-lease principal; full-year 2026 capex guidance was $130B-$145B.
Reality Labs lost $4.619B from operations in Q2 2026 and $8.647B in H1 2026; the 2025 10-K reported a $19.193B full-year RL operating loss and expected 2026 losses to remain similar.
META closed at $741.25 on September 21, 2026, the frozen valuation price.

Using the harness-locked 9% required return and 15x/20x/25x terminal multiples, the unchanged 10-year owner-FCF/share paths imply about $267 Bear, $638 Base and $1,091 Bull value. At $741.25, price/Base is about 1.161x.
evidence.source: Harness locked owner-FCF/share DCF using frozen META inputs

counterevidence: The Base path requires owner FCF/share to recover from $14 in year 1 to $54 in year 10 even while Meta is committing to exceptionally high AI infrastructure spending; sustained capex intensity would make Base too optimistic.
Q2 2026 operating margin fell to 31% from 43% a year earlier as costs grew 55%, showing that revenue growth does not automatically translate into near-term owner cash flow.
Reality Labs continues to absorb roughly $19B-$20B of annual operating profit with limited revenue, and management says the adverse financial impact may persist.
The current price is about 16.1% above Base intrinsic value at the locked 9% hurdle, so the margin for Base-case execution error is smaller than on September 18.
unknowns: Meta does not disclose a decision-useful split of 2026-2030 infrastructure spending between economically maintenance-like capex and growth capex; Q2 filings/IR were reviewed, but this remains the largest uncertainty in owner-FCF normalization.
A reproducible 5-year self-valuation percentile was not frozen, so valuation_percentile_5y remains null rather than being inferred from a secondary chart.

uncertainties.rationale: Current price is only modestly above Base value, but the implied burden still depends on the durability of the assumed post-2026 FCF recovery.
The 9% hurdle Base value is below market price; small changes in the owner-FCF recovery path materially alter the expectation gap.
Base terminal concentration is below the harness review threshold, but the maintenance-versus-growth character of AI capex is unresolved.

falsifiers: Company-defined FCF remains below roughly $30B through 2028 despite continued double-digit revenue growth, indicating the assumed cash-conversion recovery is not occurring.
Advertising growth falls to low-single digits while average price per ad and impressions both stagnate for several quarters.
Reality Labs losses materially exceed the roughly $20B annual run-rate without evidence of a credible revenue or strategic payoff.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: The frozen price of $741.25 remains below the harness-computed Bull value of about $1,091; the Bull-price veto is therefore not triggered.
